'''Kiran Sridhara Kedlaya''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|k|ɪr|ən|_|ˈ|ʃ|r|iː|d|ər|_|k|ɛ|d|ˈ|l|ɑː|j|ə}} {{respell|KIRR|ən|_|SHREE|dər|_|ked|LAH|yə}};<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mit.edu/~kedlaya/about-my-name.html|title = About My Name}}</ref> born July 1974) is an [[United States|American]] [[mathematician]]. He currently is a professor of mathematics and the [[Stefan E. Warschawski]] chair in mathematics<ref>{{cite web|title=Exploring the mathematical universe|url=http://aimath.org/aimnews/lmfdb/|website=American Institute of Mathematics|accessdate=2 August 2017|date=10 May 2016}}</ref> at the [[University of California, San Diego]].

==Biography==
Kiran Kedlaya was born into a [[Tulu Brahmin]] family.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://kskedlaya.org/about-my-name/|title=Kiran S. Kedlaya}}</ref> At age 16, Kedlaya won a gold medal at the [[International Mathematics Olympiad]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Silver Spring whiz kid brings home the gold |newspaper=[[Washington Times]] |date=July 20, 1990 }}</ref> which he later followed with a silver and another gold medal. While an undergraduate student at [[Harvard University|Harvard]], Kedlaya was a [[William Lowell Putnam Mathematical Competition#Putnam Fellows|three-time Putnam Fellow]] in 1993, 1994, and 1995.<ref name="MMA">{{cite web |title=Putnam Competition Individual and Team Winners |url=http://www.maa.org/programs/maa-awards/putnam-competition-individual-and-team-winners |publisher=[[Mathematical Association of America]] |access-date=December 14, 2021 |archive-date=March 12, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140312205244/http://www.maa.org/programs/maa-awards/putnam-competition-individual-and-team-winners |url-status=dead }}</ref> A 1996 article by ''[[The Harvard Crimson]]'' described him as "the best college-age student in math in the United States".<ref>{{cite news |last=Hsu |first=Geoffrey C. |title=Breaking the Curve |url=http://www.thecrimson.com/article/1996/6/6/breaking-the-curve-pbibm-statistically-significant/ |work=The Harvard Crimson |date=June 6, 1996 }}</ref>

Kedlaya was runner-up for the 1995 [[Morgan Prize]], for a paper<ref>{{cite journal |last=Kedlaya |first=Kiran S. |author-mask=3 |year=1997 |title=Large Product-Free Subsets of Finite Groups |journal=[[Journal of Combinatorial Theory]] |series=Series A |volume=77 |issue=2 |pages=339–343 |doi=10.1006/jcta.1997.2715 |doi-access=free }}</ref> in which he substantially improved on results of [[László Babai]] and [[Vera T. Sós|Vera Sós]] (1985)<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Babai |first1=László|authorlink1=László Babai |last2=Sós |first2=Vera T.|authorlink2=Vera T. Sós |title=Sidon sets in groups and induced subgraphs of Cayley graphs |journal=[[European Journal of Combinatorics]] |volume=6 |issue= 2|year=1985 |pages=101–114 |doi= 10.1016/s0195-6698(85)80001-9|doi-access=free|url=http://real.mtak.hu/110564/1/1-s2.0-S0195669885800019-main.pdf}}</ref> on the size of the largest product-free subset of a [[finite group]] of [[order of a group|order]] ''n''.

Kedlaya gave an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited talk]] at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 2010, on the topic of "Number Theory".<ref>{{cite web|title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers since 1897|url=http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByCongress.php|publisher=[[International Congress of Mathematicians]]|access-date=2013-08-15|archive-date=2017-11-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171108012153/http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByCongress.php|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2012, he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-01-27.</ref>

==Game shows==
Kedlaya was a contestant on the game show ''[[Jeopardy!]]'' in 2011, winning one episode.<ref>[http://www.j-archive.com/showgame.php?game_id=3770 Jeopardy! Archive – Show #6257, aired 2011–11–29]</ref>

* [https://books.google.com/books/about/p_adic_Differential_Equations.html?id=Enrw2kCqZOsC ''p-adic Differential Equations''], Cambridge Studies in Advanced Mathematics, Band 125, Cambridge University Press 2010<ref>{{cite journal|author=Berger, Laurent|title=Review: ''p-adic differential equations'', by Kiran Kedlaya|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (N.S.)|year=2012|volume=49|issue=3|pages=465–468|doi=10.1090/s0273-0979-2012-01371-X|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/2012-49-03/S0273-0979-2012-01371-X/S0273-0979-2012-01371-X.pdf|doi-access=free}}</ref>
* with David Savitt, [[Dinesh Thakur (mathematician)|Dinesh Thakur]], Matt Baker, [[Brian Conrad]], [[Samit Dasgupta]],  Jeremy Teitelbaum [https://books.google.com/books/about/P_adic_Geometry.html?id=SGAQvu0-Vm0C ''p-adic Geometry''], Lectures from the 2007 Arizona Winter School, American Mathematical Society 2008
* with [[Bjorn Poonen]], [[Ravi Vakil]] ''The William Lowell Putnam Mathematical Competition 1985-2000: Problems, Solutions and Commentary'', Mathematical Association of America, 2002
